title: Smartphone-based deep learning system detects glaucomatous visual field loss
summary: The iGlaucoma deep learning system used 10,784 visual fields from 5542 patients across seven Chinese centers. In Phase I it outperformed six ophthalmologists on three independent test sets (AUC 0.834-0.877); in Phase II, 649 visual fields from 437 patients at three clinics gave an AUC of 0.966, 0.954 sensitivity and 0.873 specificity.
ai_technology: iGlaucoma deep learning system on Humphrey visual field data
organization: Sun Yat-sen University (Zhongshan Ophthalmic Center); Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology

evidence.tested: Independent test sets and a separate Phase II evaluation at three clinics against expert glaucomatologists.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective diagnostic validation with expert-labelled references; the authors say the target population needs expert input; abstract only; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A deep-learning system classified visual fields as glaucomatous or not.
